idiom_name: for over the iterator protocol (__iter__ / __next__), generators and comprehensions
implementation_notes: Python's for statement calls iter() on the collection and drives the resulting iterator (__iter__, __next__, StopIteration), so a class becomes enumerable by implementing __iter__ - the enumeration message is the protocol rather than a named do: method. Generator functions and generator expressions are the modern replacement for the block-taking messages: the collect/select/inject family is covered by comprehensions and the map/filter/functools.reduce built-ins, while enumerate/zip supply an index or a partner sequence when a plain loop would have carried one. The explicit while loop with a manual index survives only for algorithms that manipulate the cursor itself.
pitfalls: Mutating a list or dict while iterating it silently skips or repeats elements instead of raising (only dict size changes raise RuntimeError); iterate over a copy or build a new collection.
Iterators are single-use: a generator object is exhausted after one walk, so a second for loop over the same object yields nothing - store the iterable, not its iterator.
A suspended generator keeps its frame and every object it references alive until it is exhausted or closed; abandoning one in a long-lived process leaks the referenced data.
